The meeting was called to order by Chair Lopez at 6:05 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Barragan, Vice Chair Apodaca, and Chair Lopez. Commissioner Garcia
and Commissioner Navas were absent. Also present were Jill Ann Arabe, Development
Services Manager; Carlos Rojas, Acting Senior Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann,
Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

THE 2023 NORWALK GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL
PROGRESS REPORT

Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.

Carlos Rojas, Acting Senior Planner, presented a report stating that after Planning
Commission consideration of this item, this document will be forwarded to the City
Council at its meeting on March 19, 2024, and then submitted to the Governor’s Office
of Planning and Research (OPR) and the Department of Housing and Community
Development (HCD) by April 1, 2024.

Mr. Rojas commented on the Circulation Element sharing that Caltrans is continuing
with the I-5 widening project; that the City continued with their annual inspection work
to repair/replace damaged curbs and gutters, sidewalks and traffic signals; that the
Transit Department continues to expand its battery-operated electric bus fleet and
infrastructure with the addition of two battery-operated buses and four corresponding
charging stations that were delivered in late 2023.

Continuing with his presentation, Mr. Rojas stated that in regards to the Housing
Element, on February 21, 2023, City Council adopted the 2021-2029 Housing Element;
that certification from the State was received in November of 2023; that for the reporting
year, the City issued building permits for the creation of 57 residential units; that the
Norwalk Housing Authority administers the Housing Voucher Program; that for this
reporting period, the Housing Authority assisted 550 families by paying their rent
through the Housing Choice Vouchers; 15 individuals with Mainstream Vouchers and
21 families with Emergency Housing Vouchers; that the Community Development Block
Grant (CDBG) Program rehabilitated 10 properties as of December 31, 2023 to benefit
low and moderate-income families; that, additionally, through the Home Investment

Partnership (HOME) funds were allocated for an affordable housing development of 66
units as of December 31, 2023.

Further, Mr. Rojas commented on the Conservation Element of the General Plan. He
indicated that the City continues to implement multiple public programs to align with the
City’s commitment of “going green”, promoting public awareness of the importance of
recycling/conservation and offering programs for its residents; that this program
includes the Used Oil Block Grant; E-waste and Shredding Events; that, through this
event, ten tons of electronic waste was diverted; that the Battery Recycling Program
continues throughout different City facilities; that Mandatory Commercial Recycling
requires that at least 50% of the discarded construction materials be diverted from
landfills; and that, for the reporting year, over 81% of the completed construction was
diverted.

Continuing with his presentation, Acting Senior Planner Rojas shared that with regards
to the Conservation Element, the City has continued to maintain and enhance its parks
and community facilities; that the following projects were completed in 2023:
Playground installation at Holifield Park, new playground at Bob White Park, new
pergola at Gerdes Park; and landscaping refurbishments to several parks in the
community.

Mr. Rojas stated that staff recommends, by minute motion, a recommendation to the
Norwalk City Council to receive and file the 2023 General Plan and Housing Element
Annual Progress Report, and direct staff to transmit the report to the Governor’s Office
of Planning and Research (OPR) and the Department of Housing and Community
Development (HCD) by April 1, 2024.

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Lopez closed the
public hearing.

As none of the Commissioners had any questions, they thanked staff for the
presentation and for the hard work that went into preparing this document.

It was moved by Vice Chair Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Barragan to
approve, by minute motion, a recommendation to the Norwalk City Council to receive
and file the 2023 Norwalk General Plan and Housing Element Annual Progress Report
and direct staff to transmit the report to the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research
(OPR) and the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD).

  1). Environmental: Consider and find the project exempt from CEQA pursuant to

  of approximately 20 acres bounded on the west by Norwalk Boulevard and the
  Santa Ana Freeway (I-5), to the south by the Santa Ana Freeway and Dace
  Street, to the east by Volunteer Avenue and to the north by Civic Center Drive.

RECOMMENDATION

That the Planning Commission:

1. Adopt Resolution No. 24-02 to recommend approval to City Council for Zoning Text

2. Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption), where
  it can be seen with certainty there is no possibility that the activity in question may have
  significant effect of the environment.

AUTHORITY

Section 17.02.260.D of the NMC stipulates that the Planning Commission render its
recommendation on a Zoning Text Amendment, including the reasons for the
recommendation, to the City Council.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The SPA 1 was adopted by Ordinance No. 1267 in 1987, in order to establish objectives,
policies, regulations, development standards and review criteria for the implementation of a
compatible blend of mutually supporting land uses consisting of a multi-story hotel, a wide
array of professional offices and retail commercial uses, complementary commercial
entertainment uses and residential condominiums.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The request consists of ZTA No. 2024-01 to amend various sections of Title 17 (Zoning) of
the NMC as it relates to Article 1, SPA 1.

The proposed text amendments to SPA 1 will allow for up to two (2) hotels, modify the list of
allowable uses to include billboards and other uses, include minor text amendments to
include references to wayfinding and building identification signage, remove subsection
outlining roles and procedures for the final decision-making authority to streamline the
entitlement process and promote economic development.

ANALYSIS

SPA 1 is an area of critical importance to the long-term future of Norwalk due to its location,
size, ownership and potential where maximum effort is necessary to capitalize on these
opportunities. The proposed project is consistent with the objective of SPA 1 and anticipated
to expand development opportunities in the area. The proposed text amendments are
necessary in effectuating and facilitating such opportunities by updating the list of uses,
allowing for certain signage, and streamlining the entitlement process within SPA 1.

Zoning Text Amendment

The text amendment consists of the following components:

•  Allow for a second hotel. Currently, SPA 1 limits the number of hotels to only one. The
  inclusion of a second hotel provides greater flexibility and allows for additional
  development opportunities.

•  Expand the allowable uses to include, but not limited to: billboards, arcades, bowling alley,
  entertainment venues, museums, outdoor events, restaurants, lounges and clubs.
  Currently, SPA 1 prohibits billboards. The proposed language will allow for a billboard

  and include new uses that complement the existing establishments within SPA 1 and will
  enhance the appeal and attraction of the area for economic development opportunities.

•  The proposed text amendment will update the list of prohibited uses to remove uses that
  are outdated or inconsistent with the objective of SPA 1. These uses include: collection
  agencies, credit services, detective and protective services, manufacturing and
  commercial services, security and commodity brokers, dealers and exchanges, tax
  consultation, and telephone answering service.

•  Minor text amendments will include references to wayfinding (directional) and building
  identification signage. Wayfinding and modifications to on premise and off premise
  wayfinding signage will be allowed through the Director Approval Request (DAR) process.

•  The proposed text amendment will simplify and streamline the entitlement process by
  modifying the roles and procedures for final decision-making authority which will further
  facilitate development.

Public Notification

Notice of this public hearing was published in The Norwalk Patriot and posted at the City’s
three designated posting sites and the city website on June 14, 2024.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

 The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption), where it can be seen
with certainty there is no possibility that the activity in question may have significant effect of
the environment.

SUMMARY

The proposed ZTA, which involves modifying SPA 1 and related provisions from the NMC,
will allow for a second hotel, allow for a billboard and additional compatible uses, remove
outdated uses, delineate an approval process for wayfinding signage and streamline the
entitlement approval process to encourage healthy development in a timely manner. SPA 1
is of critical importance to the long-term viability of Norwalk whereby it is critical to continue to
facilitate and encourage economic development opportunities in the area. Therefore, Staff
recommends that the Planning Commission recommend approval of the project to City
Council.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

A Special Sign District is an effective Planning tool and serves as an overlay containing
multiple parcels reasonably grouped together that would allow for the approval of a
freestanding sign. Freestanding signs are desirable to the City of Norwalk (“City”) as they
provide opportunities to enhance the urban aesthetics and promote effective
communication through controlled and cohesive signage and to provide a reasonable and
effective means of business promotion in areas where unique constraints in the built or
natural environment exist.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

City staff-initiated proposal, ZTA No. 2024-02, establishes a review process for the
creation of a Special Sign District. A Special Sign District must include multiple parcels
reasonably grouped together. Development standards for the sign(s) shall be
incorporated within the Special Sign District’s Ordinance. The proposal requires the
following minimum requirements:

·  Shall only include parcels within Specific Plan Area (SPA) 1, SPA 16, mixed-use,
  commercial, institutional and public facility overlay zone districts;

·  Minimum combined land area shall be five (5) acres;

·  Parcels shall be contiguous (but may be separated by a railroad or public street); and

·  Existing Uses shall include one (1) or more of the following: vehicle sales and lease
  (general new and used), hotels and motels (with 100 or more rooms) or a retail tenant
  (with a minimum area of 10,000 square feet).

There are no specific sign guidelines established with this proposal. Sign design
guidelines will be reviewed when a Special Sign District request is received. The review
and approval process for a proposed Special Sign District requires approval by City
Council.

ANALYSIS

The proposed zoning text amendment provides an opportunity for multiple parcels to form
a district and share a sign structure. Special Sign District requires the parcels be
substantial in combined size and anchored with a major retail tenant, vehicle sales use
or hotel/motel use. The minimum requirements to form a district are intended to ensure
that a Special Sign District is significant in both size and economic impact within the city.

This project is exempt by the provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act

known as the “Common Sense Exemption” and Section 15311 (Class 11 – Accessory
Structures) of the California Code of Regulations, for the construction or replacement of

Public Notification

Notice of this public hearing was published in The Norwalk Patriot and posted at the City’s
three designated posting sites and the City website on June 14, 2024.

SUMMARY

Staff finds the purpose of a Special Sign District aligns with the goals and policies set
forth in the General Plan and will provide additional economic tools for business to utilize
to expand commerce in the City. The proposed text amendment establishes the City
Council as the appropriate review authority for a Special Sign District and establishes the
minimum criteria for the formation of such a district. Therefore, staff recommends that the
Planning Commission recommend approval of Zoning Text Amendment No. 2024-02.

§ 17.02.255 Special Sign District.
  A. Purpose. This Subsection sets forth regulations for the establishment of Special Sign
  Districts in areas of the City containing multiple parcels that may be reasonably grouped,
  the unique characteristics of which can be enhanced by the imposition of special sign
  guidelines and standards designed to enhance the theme or unique qualities of a certain
  area, or which reinforce the identity of certain areas of the City to promote business and
  strengthen the City’s tax base and to implement the General Plan.
  B. Establishment of Special Sign Districts. The City Council, the Planning Commission or the
  Community Development Director may initiate consideration of a proposed Ordinance to
  establish a Special Sign District as set forth in Section 17.02.290 (Zone Changes) of this
  Title. Special Sign Districts shall be considered an overlay zone to modify the underlying
  zoning district with regards to signage regulations, specifically with regards to freestanding
  signs.
  C. General requirements. All signs displayed in a Special Sign District shall comply with the
  provisions of this Chapter, except as set for this in this Subsection.
  E. Minimum requirements:
  1. Zoning. Shall only include parcels in Specific Plan Area 1, Specific Plan Area 16,
  mixed-use, commercial, institutional and public facility overlay zoning districts. Shall
  not include parcels in residential zoning districts.
  2. Land area. The minimum area shall be five (5) acres.
  3. Land configuration. Shall include contiguous parcels of land, which may only be
  separated by a railroad or public street.
  4. Anchor business/tenant. The Special Sign District shall be one (1) or more of the
  following uses: vehicle sales and lease (general new and used), hotels and motels
  (with 100 and more rooms) or a retail tenant (with a minimum area of 10,000 square
  feet).
  5. Development standards. All development standards shall be determined at the time
  the Special Sign District is established and incorporated within the Special Sign
  District’s Ordinance.

AUTHORITY

Proposed Section 17.02.255 to the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) allowing for the
creation of Special Sign Districts.

Section 65855 of the California Government Code states that the Planning Commission
shall make a written recommendation on the adoption or amendment of the Zoning
Ordinance.

Section 17.02.260.D of the NMC stipulates that the Planning Commission render its
recommendation on a Zoning Text Amendment, including the reasons for the
recommendation, to the City Council.

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

In 2023, City Council adopted the Norwalk Entertainment District - Civic Center Specific
Plan Area 16 (SPA 16). SPA 16 is located at the southeast corner of Imperial Highway
and Norwalk Boulevard in Norwalk. The development of this area is anticipated to be
implemented through one or more leases to a private developer of all or a portion of the
portion of the City owned land and other contractual arrangements between the City and
a private developer.

The aim of SPA 16 is to advance the City’s goals for the plan area including the Civic
Center as an economic node to enhance the area as a thriving and experience-oriented
center for residents and visitors. SPA 16 capitalizes on the area and its close proximity to
major transportation nodes to establish a vibrant regional destination and draw for the
area. SPA 16 requires the developer to submit a Master Sign Plan for the area which will
allow for flexibility by recognizing the unique aspects of the mixed-use center and need
for various sign types and placement opportunities while ensuring consistency and quality
of design.

Specific Plan Area 1 (SPA 1) is located to the south of SPA 16. The SPA 1 parcels
included in this proposal comprise the AMC Theater, retail pad tenants and the Outback
Steakhouse. Currently there is one existing freestanding sign located in Assessor Parcel
No. 8047-007-191, (the Outback Steakhouse) that would be located within the boundary
of proposed SD 1. The Outback Steakhouse and the City of Norwalk currently have sign
panels on the existing freestanding structure, which was constructed in 1999. The
freestanding sign is 70 feet in height.

The existing height and location of the existing freestanding sign is not optimal given the
existing conditions. Expansions and improvements to Interstate-5 Freeway have
diminished the visibility of the existing freestanding sign. Additionally, the existing sign is
located within the Caltrans right-of- way and is therefore subject to Caltrans requirements
for off-premise signs. Establishing the proposed SD 1 would modify Caltrans authority

Presented concurrently with this request is ZTA 2024-02, a City staff-initiated request to
amend the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) to allow for the creation of Special Sign
Districts and establish minimum requirements for those newly created districts. ZTA 2024-
02 amends Chapter 17.02, Article V (Discretionary Approvals and Permits) of the NMC
to enable the creation of Special Sign Districts with specified criteria. These districts
require approval by the City Council, must contain multiple parcels reasonably grouped
together, and meet the following requirements:

  •  Newly created sign districts shall be limited to properties within SPA 1, SPA 16,
  mixed-use, commercial, institutional areas or public facility overlay zones;
  •  Minimum combined land area shall be five (5) acres;
  •  Parcels shall be contiguous (but may be separated by a railroad or public street);
  and
  •  Existing Uses shall include one (1) or more of the following: vehicle sales and lease
  (general new and used), hotels and motels (with 100 or more rooms) or a retail
  tenant (with a minimum of area of 10,000 square feet).
  •  All development standards shall be determined at the time the Special Sign District
  is established and incorporated within the Special Sign District’s Ordinance.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
Zone Change No. 2024-01 is a request to establish the Special Sign District No. 01 (SD
1) overlay. SD 1 is comprised of 11 non- residential properties, located within in the SPA
1, SPA 16, Institutional and Public Facility overlay zone districts. SD 1 includes the
following parcels listed in no particular order by assessor parcel numbers: 8047-006-910,
8047-006-922, 8047-006-924, 8047-006-925, 8047-006-926, 8047-006-927, 8047-007-
136, 8047-007-188, 8047-007-189, 8047-007-190 and 8047-007-191.

Zoning Text Amendment No. 2024-03 proposes to amend Title 17 (Zoning), Chapter
17.01 (Administration), Article II (Establishment of Zones, and limiting the Uses of Land
Therein) and Title 17 (Zoning), Chapter 17.03 (Development Requirements), Article III
(Signs) to establish SD 1 development standards and allow one freeway-oriented on-
premise freestanding sign greater than 35 feet.

ANALYSIS

Per § 17.03.140 of the NMC, freestanding signs are permitted in the C-1, C-3, C-M, M-1
and M-2 zones, subject to the approval of a sign use permit. Freestanding signs are

  limited to a maximum height limit of 35 feet above finished grade, or as otherwise
  determined by an approved Sign Use Permit.

  The proposed development standards for the on-premise freestanding signs would allow
  for a greater height maximum to account for elevation differences between the proposed
  sign location and Interstate-5 Freeway. The Interstate-5 Freeway lanes are elevated at
  the existing Norwalk Boulevard underpass. Allowing for a 100-foot freestanding sign
  would counter the change in elevation and provide adequate exposure for vehicles driving
  in the northbound and southbound lanes to view signage along the frontage area. The
  proposed SD 1 development standards will allow replacement of the existing on-premise
  sign with a taller freestanding sign to advertise uses within the SD 1 boundary.

  The formation of a SD 1 will allow businesses entities within the Norwalk Entertainment
  District (SPA 16) more flexibility for their signage when submitted as part of their future
  Master Sign Program.

  ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

  The proposed Resolution is exempt by the provisions of the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to Sections 15061(b)(3) of the California Code of
  Regulations, also known as the “Common Sense Exemption” and 15311 (Class 11 –
  Accessory Structures), for the construction or replacement of minor accessory structures
  including on-premise signs. A public notice was prepared and published in the local
  newspaper. Four (4) notices were posted on or in proximity to the subject parcels. Any
  future project subject to the SD 1 provisions shall undergo its own independent
  environmental review for compliance.

  SUMMARY

  Staff finds the purpose of ZC No. 2024-01 and ZTA No. 2024-03 objectives and standards
  in line with the goals and policies of the General Plan and in compliance with the
  regulations within the City of Norwalk Municipal Code. Establishing the SD 1 boundary
  area, as shown in Attachment A, and the development standards, as shown in Attachment
  B, will serve as an effective tool to allow one on-premise freestanding sign oriented
  towards the freeway. Such signs are desirable to the City as they provide opportunities
  to enhance urban aesthetics and promote effective communication through controlled and
  cohesive signage.

§ 17.03.210 Special Sign District No. 01.

A.  Purpose.
  The City has adopted this Special Sign District No. 01 (SD 1) in accordance with
  the provisions of Chapter Title 17 Chapter 17.02 Article V of the Norwalk Municipal
  Code (NMC) in order to demolish an existing freeway-oriented freestanding sign
  and construct a new freeway-oriented freestanding sign that would enhance the
  economic vitality of the businesses within SD 1.

B.  Applicability.

  This Special Sign District applies to 8047-006-910, 8047-006-922, 8047-006-924,
  8047-006-925, 8047-006-926, 8047-006-927, 8047-007-136, 8047-007-188,
  8047-007-189, 8047-007-190 and 8047-007-191.

C.  District Boundaries:

  The boundaries of SD 1 are reflected within the Zoning Map.

D.  Development standards:

  1) One (1) static freestanding freeway-oriented sign up to 100 feet tall
  shall be permitted.
  2) Proposed sign may be illuminated or non-illuminated.
  3) May have a maximum width of 30 feet.
  4) May have a maximum number of six (6) sign panels for up to six (6)
  tenants.

E.  Approvals:

  1. Relation to Signage Regulations. Any person desiring to erect or place a sign
  on the new freeway- oriented freestanding sign shall comply with all provisions
  of Chapter 17.03 Article III Signs of the NMC unless specifically modified
  herein.

   2. Location of Businesses Allowed on a Freeway- Oriented Freestanding Sign. The
  business shall be located within the boundary of SD 1. No other business, product,
  service or use shall be permitted on the freestanding sign.

  3. Sign Permit Required. A Sign Permit as provided in Section 17.03 of the NMC
  shall be required for any sign face change (including new businesses).

F.  Administration and General Provisions:

  1. Review of Final Designs. The Planning Commission shall review and approve
  the final design for any new sign subject to this provision via a Sign Use Permit.

  2. Other Requirements May Still Apply. Nothing in this Special Sign District
  ordinance eliminates the need for obtaining any other approval or entitlement
  required by provisions of the NMC or any local, State or Federal agency.

G.  Responsibility for Administration. The Community Development Director, or
  designee, shall be responsible for administering the provisions of SD 1. This shall
  include the responsibility and authority to interpret any section of this document.
